Large scale storage is a

properties.name: Cumulus Energy Storage
properties.description:
Cumulus Energy Storage (Cumulus) aims to be the leading manufacturer and developer of grid-level rechargeable Copper/Zinc energy storage batteries with the lowest levelised cost of storage (LCOS) globally.

Large scale storage is an essential part of the future of energy. We need electricity super-storage to give industry the freedom of instantly available renewable electricity; give grid the capacity to deliver security of supply; and give time-shifting to renewables so that solar energy after sunset becomes reality.

The market drivers for energy storage are set in legislation. Increasing distributed renewables generation, especially the recent growth in solar PV on top of onshore and offshore wind, is causing pain points for grid infrastructure and incumbent generators; creating urgent global need for reliable low-cost, scalable grid-level energy storage.

Cumulus has taken the bold and visionary step of combining a 200 year old technology from one industry, with technology from two other industrial-scale processes, to create a disruptive opportunity – electricity super-storage – using patent granted technology in the form of a low-cost grid-scale rechargeable Copper/Zinc battery.

With financial support from the UK government and investment from business angels, Cumulus has extended from Sheffield to San Francisco, with laboratory facilities developing grid-connected full-scale prototypes. Pilot line production, followed by full production capacity, is supported by global component manufacturers and continental forming and assembly plants; delivering our super-storage products and services to customers through local project developers.

Advanced Battery Technology: Utilize cutting-edge battery technology, such as solid-state batteries, to improve energy density, charging/discharging efficiency, and overall system longevity. Decentralized Network: Establish a decentralized network of ESS units that can be deployed at various scales - from residential homes to industrial facilities. These units will be interconnected through the Internet of Things (IoT) for real-time monitoring and control.

Renewable Integration: Prioritize the integration of renewable energy sources, such as solar and wind, into the ESS network. Linkz ESS units can store excess energy generated during peak production times and release it when renewable sources are less productive, ensuring a continuous and reliable energy supply.

properties.name: JoinB2B

The main mission of JoinB2B is to directly and without any mediator match the relevant companies to each other. 
But, how JoinB2B determines which company fits any other specific company? For that, JoinB2B utilizes belowmentioned methods:

JoinB2B matches the companies depending on their own as well as target locations.
It is not surprising that most companies have their target locations for enlarging their businesses along with their location of their operations. For example, if Company “A” selected its location as Germany, Berlin and its target location as Hungary, Budapest while Company “B” selected its location as Hungary, Budapest and its target location as Germany Berlin, then the unique matching system of JoinB2B introduces these two companies to each other. 

JoinB2B matches the companies depending on their business purpose. 

When registering at JoinB2B, the companies are asked about their registration purpose (B2B purpose). For example, if company “A” selected its B2B purpose as “to find a sub-contractor”, while company ”B” selected its B2B purpose as “to become a sub-contractor”, then the unique matching system of JoinB2B introduces these two companies to each other. The companies are able to see the list of the companies matching their B2B purpose easily at the right side of the website. 

JoinB2B matches the companies depending on products/services that they offer and products/services that they demand.

For example, if company “A” is offering a pen while company “B” announces a tender for purchasing a pen, then the system will automatically introduce these two companies to each other. System matches these two companies because their offers and demands are relevant to each other. 

Join B2B provides messaging services to its users to help them to directly, without any obstacles contact each other.

properties.name: Infozeb

Infozeb is a deep-tech engineering company building India's most modular Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) platform — designed, built, and finished in India.
We design and manufacture BESS that scale from a 3 kW residential wall-mount to a 2 MW containerised utility asset, all on one platform. One firmware family, one BMS architecture, one supply chain — service one, service all.
What sets us apart is that we own the entire stack. The battery management system, power conversion, energy management, the on-unit HMI, and the cloud monitoring platform are all proprietary in-house IP — no third-party black boxes. Our systems charge from solar, wind, and grid, and deliver single-phase AC, three-phase AC, and DC output, replacing the solar inverter, the diesel generator, the grid-tie, and the DC supply in a single hybrid platform. Built on LiFePO4 cells rated for 6,000 cycles, with a chemistry-agnostic pack architecture ready for NMC and sodium-ion as they mature.
Our mission is to take India off diesel — making clean, stored backup power cheaper than running a generator for every home, factory, EV charging hub, and grid edge, while cutting the nation's dependence on imported oil.
Infozeb handles engineering, manufacturing, and after-sales support. Our go-to-market partner, leads sales, deployment, and market access across India.

Cumulus Energy Storage (Cumulus) aims to be the leading manufacturer and developer of grid-level rechargeable Copper/Zinc energy storage batteries with the lowest levelised cost of storage (LCOS) globally.

Large scale storage is an essential part of the future of energy. We need electricity super-storage to give industry the freedom of instantly available renewable electricity; give grid the capacity to deliver security of supply; and give time-shifting to renewables so that solar energy after sunset becomes reality.

The market drivers for energy storage are set in legislation. Increasing distributed renewables generation, especially the recent growth in solar PV on top of onshore and offshore wind, is causing pain points for grid infrastructure and incumbent generators; creating urgent global need for reliable low-cost, scalable grid-level energy storage.

Cumulus has taken the bold and visionary step of combining a 200 year old technology from one industry, with technology from two other industrial-scale processes, to create a disruptive opportunity – electricity super-storage – using patent granted technology in the form of a low-cost grid-scale rechargeable Copper/Zinc battery.

With financial support from the UK government and investment from business angels, Cumulus has extended from Sheffield to San Francisco, with laboratory facilities developing grid-connected full-scale prototypes. Pilot line production, followed by full production capacity, is supported by global component manufacturers and continental forming and assembly plants; delivering our super-storage products and services to customers through local project developers.

entity.name: Linkz ESS
entity.description:
"Linkz ESS: Empowering the Future of Energy Storage Solutions"

Introduction:
In the rapidly evolving landscape of energy production and consumption, the integration of Energy Storage Systems (ESS) is becoming increasingly vital. Linkz ESS aims to be at the forefront of this transformative journey by revolutionizing how we harness and distribute energy. Our vision is to create an interconnected network of smart ESS units that not only store excess energy efficiently but also contribute to the growth of renewable energy sources. Here's an idea of how Linkz ESS can shape the future of ESS and new energy:

Key Components:

Advanced Battery Technology: Utilize cutting-edge battery technology, such as solid-state batteries, to improve energy density, charging/discharging efficiency, and overall system longevity. These innovations will enable rapid energy storage and release when needed, reducing waste and increasing overall system reliability.

Decentralized Network: Establish a decentralized network of ESS units that can be deployed at various scales - from residential homes to industrial facilities. These units will be interconnected through the Internet of Things (IoT) for real-time monitoring and control.

AI-Driven Energy Management: Implement Artificial Intelligence (AI) algorithms for predictive energy management. This technology can optimize when and how energy is stored and released, taking into account factors like weather forecasts, energy demand patterns, and market pricing.

Renewable Integration: Prioritize the integration of renewable energy sources, such as solar and wind, into the ESS network. Linkz ESS units can store excess energy generated during peak production times and release it when renewable sources are less productive, ensuring a continuous and reliable energy supply.

The future of growth belongs to companies that deeply understand their buyers.

We help organizations build that advantage.

entity.name: JoinB2B
entity.description:
The main mission of JoinB2B is to directly and without any mediator match the relevant companies to each other. 
But, how JoinB2B determines which company fits any other specific company? For that, JoinB2B utilizes belowmentioned methods:

JoinB2B matches the companies depending on their own as well as target locations.
It is not surprising that most companies have their target locations for enlarging their businesses along with their location of their operations. For example, if Company “A” selected its location as Germany, Berlin and its target location as Hungary, Budapest while Company “B” selected its location as Hungary, Budapest and its target location as Germany Berlin, then the unique matching system of JoinB2B introduces these two companies to each other. 

JoinB2B matches the companies depending on their business purpose. 

When registering at JoinB2B, the companies are asked about their registration purpose (B2B purpose). For example, if company “A” selected its B2B purpose as “to find a sub-contractor”, while company ”B” selected its B2B purpose as “to become a sub-contractor”, then the unique matching system of JoinB2B introduces these two companies to each other. The companies are able to see the list of the companies matching their B2B purpose easily at the right side of the website. 

JoinB2B matches the companies depending on products/services that they offer and products/services that they demand.

For example, if company “A” is offering a pen while company “B” announces a tender for purchasing a pen, then the system will automatically introduce these two companies to each other. System matches these two companies because their offers and demands are relevant to each other. 

Join B2B provides messaging services to its users to help them to directly, without any obstacles contact each other.

Infozeb is a deep-tech engineering company building India's most modular Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) platform — designed, built, and finished in India.
We design and manufacture BESS that scale from a 3 kW residential wall-mount to a 2 MW containerised utility asset, all on one platform. The system is built around a single 30 kW bidirectional power module: a 60 kW unit is two modules, 480 kW is sixteen, and so on. One firmware family, one BMS architecture, one supply chain — service one, service all.
What sets us apart is that we own the entire stack. The battery management system, power conversion, energy management, the on-unit HMI, and the cloud monitoring platform are all proprietary in-house IP — no third-party black boxes. Our systems charge from solar, wind, and grid, and deliver single-phase AC, three-phase AC, and DC output, replacing the solar inverter, the diesel generator, the grid-tie, and the DC supply in a single hybrid platform. Built on LiFePO4 cells rated for 6,000 cycles, with a chemistry-agnostic pack architecture ready for NMC and sodium-ion as they mature.
Our mission is to take India off diesel — making clean, stored backup power cheaper than running a generator for every home, factory, EV charging hub, and grid edge, while cutting the nation's dependence on imported oil.
Infozeb handles engineering, manufacturing, and after-sales support. Our go-to-market partner, leads sales, deployment, and market access across India.

📍 Gurugram, Haryana, India

messages.content:
You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B benchmark.

Definition - a company lookalike API takes a seed company and returns other
companies that resemble it. Resemblance has two halves, and they are judged
DIFFERENTLY:

  ANCHOR       - who the seed sells to, and what it fundamentally is
                 (e.g. "restaurant point-of-sale platform"). This is a HARD
                 requirement. Every lookalike must be the same kind of company
                 for the same kind of customer. No amount of feature overlap
                 substitutes for it.
  CAPABILITIES - what the seed does (e.g. payments, online ordering, payroll,
                 operations). A lookalike matches ANY non-empty subset. It does
                 not need all of them, and matching more is not required to
                 qualify - only to be a closer match.

So: a true lookalike clears the ANCHOR and shares at least one CAPABILITY.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company - the company the lookalike search started from, with its
    ANCHOR and its CAPABILITIES listed separately.
  • A CANDIDATE company - a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide in this order, and do not work backwards from a conclusion:

STEP 1 - anchor_match (the gate).
  True only if the CANDIDATE is the same kind of company as the ANCHOR, for
  the same kind of customer. Ask: would someone shopping for the SEED consider
  this company to be in the same market?
    - A different customer fails, even in the same product category
      (restaurant POS vs retail-only POS: the customer differs).
    - A different category fails, even for the same customer
      (a restaurant POS vs a restaurant-supply distributor: both sell to
      restaurants, but only one is the same kind of company).
    - Serving the category rather than competing in it fails: agencies,
      consultancies, integrators, resellers.
    - Being a customer of the category fails (an actual restaurant is not a
      lookalike of a restaurant POS platform).
    - Parent/holding companies, the seed itself, and duplicate or parody
      entries fail.
  When you cannot tell what the candidate sells, anchor_match is false.

STEP 2 - capabilities_matched (the overlap).
  List the SEED capabilities this candidate also does, copying the strings
  verbatim from the SEED's list. Include a capability when the candidate
  plausibly offers it as part of its product; leave it out when you have no
  evidence. Matching a subset is normal and expected.

STEP 3 - relevant.
  relevant = anchor_match AND capabilities_matched is non-empty.
  Nothing else changes it.

Rules that apply throughout:
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. A smaller, larger, or
    differently-located company clears the anchor if it is the same kind of
    company for the same kind of customer. Ignore such metadata.
  - A shared generic taxonomy label or keyword is not an anchor match. Neither
    is a similar technology stack - tech co-signals may support a judgement but
    never establish one.
  - Judge the candidate's primary business, not a side feature.
  - When in doubt on the anchor, answer false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words: name the anchor verdict and the overlap.

Worked examples (SEED anchor -> candidate -> verdict):
  - "restaurant point-of-sale platform" [payments, online ordering, payroll]
      • a restaurant POS suite with payments and online ordering
        -> anchor true, matched [payments, online ordering], relevant true.
      • a restaurant POS with none of the listed capabilities
        -> anchor true, matched [], relevant FALSE (no overlap).
      • a retail-only POS with payments
        -> anchor FALSE (different customer), relevant false.
      • a general payments processor with no restaurant POS product
        -> anchor FALSE (different category), relevant false.
      • an actual restaurant chain
        -> anchor FALSE (customer of the category), relevant false.
      • an agency that installs restaurant POS systems
        -> anchor FALSE (serves the category), relevant false.
  - "CRM and marketing automation platform for go-to-market teams"
      • a smaller CRM with marketing automation -> anchor true, relevant true.
      • a lead-generation agency using that CRM for clients -> anchor false.
  - "digital bank for consumers"
      • a digital bank in another country -> anchor true (geography is not a
        constraint), relevant true if any capability overlaps.
  - "developer-security platform"
      • a company on a similar cloud stack selling HR software -> anchor false.

Definition - a company lookalike API takes a seed company and returns other
companies that resemble it. Resemblance has two halves, and they are judged
DIFFERENTLY:

  ANCHOR       - who the seed sells to, and what it fundamentally is
                 (e.g. "restaurant point-of-sale platform"). This is a HARD
                 requirement. Every lookalike must be the same kind of company
                 for the same kind of customer. No amount of feature overlap
                 substitutes for it.
  CAPABILITIES - what the seed does (e.g. payments, online ordering, payroll,
                 operations). A lookalike matches ANY non-empty subset. It does
                 not need all of them, and matching more is not required to
                 qualify - only to be a closer match.

So: a true lookalike clears the ANCHOR and shares at least one CAPABILITY.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company - the company the lookalike search started from, with its
    ANCHOR and its CAPABILITIES listed separately.
  • A CANDIDATE company - a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide in this order, and do not work backwards from a conclusion:

STEP 1 - anchor_match (the gate).
  True only if the CANDIDATE is the same kind of company as the ANCHOR, for
  the same kind of customer. Ask: would someone shopping for the SEED consider
  this company to be in the same market?
    - A different customer fails, even in the same product category
      (restaurant POS vs retail-only POS: the customer differs).
    - A different category fails, even for the same customer
      (a restaurant POS vs a restaurant-supply distributor: both sell to
      restaurants, but only one is the same kind of company).
    - Serving the category rather than competing in it fails: agencies,
      consultancies, integrators, resellers.
    - Being a customer of the category fails (an actual restaurant is not a
      lookalike of a restaurant POS platform).
    - Parent/holding companies, the seed itself, and duplicate or parody
      entries fail.
  When you cannot tell what the candidate sells, anchor_match is false.

STEP 2 - capabilities_matched (the overlap).
  List the SEED capabilities this candidate also does, copying the strings
  verbatim from the SEED's list. Include a capability when the candidate
  plausibly offers it as part of its product; leave it out when you have no
  evidence. Matching a subset is normal and expected.

STEP 3 - relevant.
  relevant = anchor_match AND capabilities_matched is non-empty.
  Nothing else changes it.

Rules that apply throughout:
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. A smaller, larger, or
    differently-located company clears the anchor if it is the same kind of
    company for the same kind of customer. Ignore such metadata.
  - A shared generic taxonomy label or keyword is not an anchor match. Neither
    is a similar technology stack - tech co-signals may support a judgement but
    never establish one.
  - Judge the candidate's primary business, not a side feature.
  - When in doubt on the anchor, answer false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words: name the anchor verdict and the overlap.

Worked examples (SEED anchor -> candidate -> verdict):
  - "restaurant point-of-sale platform" [payments, online ordering, payroll]
      • a restaurant POS suite with payments and online ordering
        -> anchor true, matched [payments, online ordering], relevant true.
      • a restaurant POS with none of the listed capabilities
        -> anchor true, matched [], relevant FALSE (no overlap).
      • a retail-only POS with payments
        -> anchor FALSE (different customer), relevant false.
      • a general payments processor with no restaurant POS product
        -> anchor FALSE (different category), relevant false.
      • an actual restaurant chain
        -> anchor FALSE (customer of the category), relevant false.
      • an agency that installs restaurant POS systems
        -> anchor FALSE (serves the category), relevant false.
  - "CRM and marketing automation platform for go-to-market teams"
      • a smaller CRM with marketing automation -> anchor true, relevant true.
      • a lead-generation agency using that CRM for clients -> anchor false.
  - "digital bank for consumers"
      • a digital bank in another country -> anchor true (geography is not a
        constraint), relevant true if any capability overlaps.
  - "developer-security platform"
      • a company on a similar cloud stack selling HR software -> anchor false.

Definition - a company lookalike API takes a seed company and returns other
companies that resemble it. Resemblance has two halves, and they are judged
DIFFERENTLY:

  ANCHOR       - who the seed sells to, and what it fundamentally is
                 (e.g. "restaurant point-of-sale platform"). This is a HARD
                 requirement. Every lookalike must be the same kind of company
                 for the same kind of customer. No amount of feature overlap
                 substitutes for it.
  CAPABILITIES - what the seed does (e.g. payments, online ordering, payroll,
                 operations). A lookalike matches ANY non-empty subset. It does
                 not need all of them, and matching more is not required to
                 qualify - only to be a closer match.

So: a true lookalike clears the ANCHOR and shares at least one CAPABILITY.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company - the company the lookalike search started from, with its
    ANCHOR and its CAPABILITIES listed separately.
  • A CANDIDATE company - a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide in this order, and do not work backwards from a conclusion:

STEP 1 - anchor_match (the gate).
  True only if the CANDIDATE is the same kind of company as the ANCHOR, for
  the same kind of customer. Ask: would someone shopping for the SEED consider
  this company to be in the same market?
    - A different customer fails, even in the same product category
      (restaurant POS vs retail-only POS: the customer differs).
    - A different category fails, even for the same customer
      (a restaurant POS vs a restaurant-supply distributor: both sell to
      restaurants, but only one is the same kind of company).
    - Serving the category rather than competing in it fails: agencies,
      consultancies, integrators, resellers.
    - Being a customer of the category fails (an actual restaurant is not a
      lookalike of a restaurant POS platform).
    - Parent/holding companies, the seed itself, and duplicate or parody
      entries fail.
  When you cannot tell what the candidate sells, anchor_match is false.

STEP 2 - capabilities_matched (the overlap).
  List the SEED capabilities this candidate also does, copying the strings
  verbatim from the SEED's list. Include a capability when the candidate
  plausibly offers it as part of its product; leave it out when you have no
  evidence. Matching a subset is normal and expected.

STEP 3 - relevant.
  relevant = anchor_match AND capabilities_matched is non-empty.
  Nothing else changes it.

Rules that apply throughout:
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. A smaller, larger, or
    differently-located company clears the anchor if it is the same kind of
    company for the same kind of customer. Ignore such metadata.
  - A shared generic taxonomy label or keyword is not an anchor match. Neither
    is a similar technology stack - tech co-signals may support a judgement but
    never establish one.
  - Judge the candidate's primary business, not a side feature.
  - When in doubt on the anchor, answer false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words: name the anchor verdict and the overlap.

Worked examples (SEED anchor -> candidate -> verdict):
  - "restaurant point-of-sale platform" [payments, online ordering, payroll]
      • a restaurant POS suite with payments and online ordering
        -> anchor true, matched [payments, online ordering], relevant true.
      • a restaurant POS with none of the listed capabilities
        -> anchor true, matched [], relevant FALSE (no overlap).
      • a retail-only POS with payments
        -> anchor FALSE (different customer), relevant false.
      • a general payments processor with no restaurant POS product
        -> anchor FALSE (different category), relevant false.
      • an actual restaurant chain
        -> anchor FALSE (customer of the category), relevant false.
      • an agency that installs restaurant POS systems
        -> anchor FALSE (serves the category), relevant false.
  - "CRM and marketing automation platform for go-to-market teams"
      • a smaller CRM with marketing automation -> anchor true, relevant true.
      • a lead-generation agency using that CRM for clients -> anchor false.
  - "digital bank for consumers"
      • a digital bank in another country -> anchor true (geography is not a
        constraint), relevant true if any capability overlaps.
  - "developer-security platform"
      • a company on a similar cloud stack selling HR software -> anchor false.

messages.content:
You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B benchmark.

Definition - a company lookalike API takes a seed company and returns other
companies that resemble it. Resemblance has two halves, and they are judged
DIFFERENTLY:

  ANCHOR       - who the seed sells to, and what it fundamentally is
                 (e.g. "restaurant point-of-sale platform"). This is a HARD
                 requirement. Every lookalike must be the same kind of company
                 for the same kind of customer. No amount of feature overlap
                 substitutes for it.
  CAPABILITIES - what the seed does (e.g. payments, online ordering, payroll,
                 operations). A lookalike matches ANY non-empty subset. It does
                 not need all of them, and matching more is not required to
                 qualify - only to be a closer match.

So: a true lookalike clears the ANCHOR and shares at least one CAPABILITY.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company - the company the lookalike search started from, with its
    ANCHOR and its CAPABILITIES listed separately.
  • A CANDIDATE company - a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide in this order, and do not work backwards from a conclusion:

STEP 1 - anchor_match (the gate).
  True only if the CANDIDATE is the same kind of company as the ANCHOR, for
  the same kind of customer. Ask: would someone shopping for the SEED consider
  this company to be in the same market?
    - A different customer fails, even in the same product category
      (restaurant POS vs retail-only POS: the customer differs).
    - A different category fails, even for the same customer
      (a restaurant POS vs a restaurant-supply distributor: both sell to
      restaurants, but only one is the same kind of company).
    - Serving the category rather than competing in it fails: agencies,
      consultancies, integrators, resellers.
    - Being a customer of the category fails (an actual restaurant is not a
      lookalike of a restaurant POS platform).
    - Parent/holding companies, the seed itself, and duplicate or parody
      entries fail.
  When you cannot tell what the candidate sells, anchor_match is false.

STEP 2 - capabilities_matched (the overlap).
  List the SEED capabilities this candidate also does, copying the strings
  verbatim from the SEED's list. Include a capability when the candidate
  plausibly offers it as part of its product; leave it out when you have no
  evidence. Matching a subset is normal and expected.

STEP 3 - relevant.
  relevant = anchor_match AND capabilities_matched is non-empty.
  Nothing else changes it.

Rules that apply throughout:
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. A smaller, larger, or
    differently-located company clears the anchor if it is the same kind of
    company for the same kind of customer. Ignore such metadata.
  - A shared generic taxonomy label or keyword is not an anchor match. Neither
    is a similar technology stack - tech co-signals may support a judgement but
    never establish one.
  - Judge the candidate's primary business, not a side feature.
  - When in doubt on the anchor, answer false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words: name the anchor verdict and the overlap.

        -> anchor FALSE (different customer), relevant false.
      • a general payments processor with no restaurant POS product
        -> anchor FALSE (different category), relevant false.
      • an actual restaurant chain
        -> anchor FALSE (customer of the category), relevant false.
      • an agency that installs restaurant POS systems
        -> anchor FALSE (serves the category), relevant false.
  - "CRM and marketing automation platform for go-to-market teams"
      • a smaller CRM with marketing automation -> anchor true, relevant true.
      • a lead-generation agency using that CRM for clients -> anchor false.
  - "digital bank for consumers"
      • a digital bank in another country -> anchor true (geography is not a
        constraint), relevant true if any capability overlaps.
  - "developer-security platform"
      • a company on a similar cloud stack selling HR software -> anchor false.
